questions.stem: What is the main function of the digestive system?

options.text: To break down large insoluble food molecules into small soluble molecules for absorption
To transport oxygen around the body

questions.explanation: The digestive system breaks down large, insoluble food molecules into small, soluble molecules that can be absorbed into the blood and used by cells.

options.text: The production of bile by the liver
The chemical breakdown of food by enzymes
The absorption of nutrients in the small intestine
The wave-like muscular contractions that push food through the digestive tract

questions.explanation: Peristalsis is the rhythmic wave-like contraction of smooth muscles in the walls of the digestive tract that pushes food along from the mouth to the anus.

questions.stem: Where does most chemical digestion and absorption take place?
questions.explanation: The small intestine is where most chemical digestion is completed (with the help of enzymes from the pancreas) and where most absorption of nutrients takes place through the villi.

questions.stem: What is the function of the stomach?

options.text: To churn food and begin protein digestion using pepsin and hydrochloric acid

questions.explanation: The stomach churns food mechanically and begins protein digestion using the enzyme pepsin, which works in the acidic conditions created by hydrochloric acid (pH ~2).

questions.stem: What does the liver produce that aids fat digestion?
questions.explanation: The liver produces bile, which is stored in the gall bladder and released into the small intestine. Bile emulsifies fats into smaller droplets, increasing the surface area for lipase to act on.

questions.stem: What is the main function of the large intestine?

options.text: To absorb water from undigested food

questions.explanation: The large intestine absorbs water and some minerals from the remaining undigested food, turning it into faeces for excretion.

questions.stem: What is the role of the pancreas in digestion?

options.text: To produce digestive enzymes (amylase, protease, lipase) and release them into the small intestine

questions.explanation: The pancreas produces and secretes digestive enzymes including amylase (for starch), protease (for protein), and lipase (for fats) into the duodenum of the small intestine.
